items.author: Cointelegraph
items.context: @Cointelegraph (2.923.893 seguidores), en inglés: "A solo miner has successfully mined a block, earning 3.178 $BTC worth about $186K." Publicado hace ~1,5 h: 108 likes, 11 reposts, 32 respuestas, ~21.000 vistas. Tema halving y emisión.
items.suggested_text:
Look at the number itself: 3.178 BTC is the 3.125 BTC block subsidy plus roughly 0.05 BTC in fees. Almost the entire reward is still newly issued coins, which tells you how little fee revenue is carrying security right now.

That split is the part to watch. At the next halving the subsidy drops to 1.5625 BTC per block, from ~450 to ~225 BTC a day across the network, and by then only 3.125% of the 21M will be left to issue.

A solo miner hitting a block is a nice lottery story. The quieter question is what a winning block is worth once the subsidy stops doing most of the work.
